summary: All twenty-four findings confirmed; many fixes are amended, and parts of /17 and /22 are rejected within the finding. /1 (high): eleven stated-result records, but only E36 and E83 reach items; E136 (item 122) is the eleventh record the finding misses, item 136 should be dropped, and E36 must go into items 46 and 61. /8 (high): two pending design jobs for AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity (and the same for BCGP25); make_queue drops only by job id, so the twin jobs and their reviews must also be superseded in queue.json by the maintainer, and DESIGN-BCGP25 needs route 12's brief attached. /3: E137's correction dropped the disjointness E140 needs, but the finding's claim that Lemma 9.2.7(6) needs it is wrong; (6) follows from full image and the determinant. /4–/7: new mistakes, all in both texts (/4 affects a stated result for F ≠ Q). /9: group Part IIs per roadmap id and order DESIGN-BCGP18 after the open-image Part II. /10: the Galois-representation half is RT-AREA-langlands-1/19; the spinor-polynomial half is new. /11: BCGP 2025's Theorem 1.8.17 is strictly stronger, so the owner must plan that form. /12–/14: owner changes confirmed (/14: G7, with Tate's H² vanishing requested from R02.4). /15–/24: confirmed with corrections (draft-packet nodes plan nothing; /18's Carayol lemma goes to IHG.1/ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7 per Calegari–Geraghty 2020; more locators lack published pages).

A GSp-conjugacy would need A^t [[0,1],[1,0]] A = cI, which is impossible because the left side is alternating. (c) E139: I counted points on y^2 + (x^3+1)y = x^2 + x over F_97 and F_97^2 and got a_1 = 10 and a_2 = 82. Then a_1^2 - 4a_2 = 63 is a non-square mod 97, so the unit roots at q = 97 are not in F_97. With a_5 = 2^4*eta^2*3 it equals the printed 2^90*3^6*(1-sqrt(-6))^30*(2-sqrt(-6))^6, and with the printed 2^4*eta*3 it does not. A pure N is the unique Weil-Deligne structure that maximises rank N^j for every j. Rank N alone characterises it when V is 4-dimensional and N is symplectic. I checked each record at its TeX line and published page, and I checked each item's text. All the printed passages are the same in both versions. No item cites its record. That Delta contains the infinite group Z_(p)^{x,+}, which acts trivially, so 'Delta acts freely' (Lemma 3.5.3) is false as printed. Items 41, 209 and 211 copy all three forms, and item 41 even states the trivial action beside the wrong stabilizer. E25 and E26: item 39 asks for a Z_(p)^x-polarization in Lan's sense, which has trivial p-kernel, and at Par(v) for a kernel of order p^2, so the moduli problem is empty at paramodular level. It also writes f^*lambda = r lambda', where f^*lambda is not defined for f: A -> A'. The direction lambda = r f^*lambda' matches eta'_2 = r^{-1} eta_2. E63: under the printed hypothesis, phi, lambda and lambda' are invertible in Hom (x) Z_(p), so x is a unit and N(x)^3 is prime to p. But Propositions 5.6.1 and 5.7.5 use N(x_w)^3/p^3 and N(x_w)^6/p^6 with x_w a uniformiser. So item 68 as stated cannot feed items 70 and 71. E52: for d = 2 (S = A^2, s = x, y), the sign (-1)^{i_j} gives d o d = -2 f-bar, which is nonzero since p > 2. The sign (-1)^j gives 0. Item 59 keeps (-1)^{i_j}. Confirmed, but the finding's explanation needs correcting before it goes into the records. I checked Proposition 9.1.12 and the proof of Lemma 9.2.7 in the TeX and in the published text. The wording is the same in both. Condition (2) is on published p. 458, not p. 459; conditions (4) and (5) are on p. 459; the sentence '(6) then follows from Lemma 7.5.22' is on p. 463. What the finding gets right. E137's correction, repeated in the route-3 brief, keeps only 'K/E linearly disjoint from E'F^(avoid)/E'. E140's reason starts from 'By Proposition 9.1.12(2), L' is linearly disjoint over K' from K'F^(avoid)' and uses it to show that psi = eps-bar * det r-bar_q maps onto F_q^x, so that the printed square-root step fails rather than merely going unjustified. Neither the printed (2), which is impossible when E' != E, nor E137's (2) gives that disjointness. So the two confirmed records rest on different versions of the proposition. Item 174 is worse: it still states the printed, impossible form (L/K Galois with L' = LE', and the printed (2)), against the rule that items use corrected statements. What the finding gets wrong. It says Lemma 9.2.7(6) needs the stronger disjointness because the hypothesis of Lemma 7.5.22 'fails if L' meets K'F^(avoid) in more than the determinant forces'. That is false. Lemma 7.5.22 needs r-bar_q(G_{K'(zeta_q)}) = SL_2(F_q), with K' = F_1F'. Suppose r-bar_q maps G_{K'} onto GL_2(F_q), which is condition (4), and det r-bar_q = eps-bar^{-1}, which is condition (3). Then G_{K'(zeta_q)} = ker(eps-bar) = ker(det o r-bar_q), and its image is exactly SL_2(F_q), however L' meets K'F^(avoid). The paper itself takes from 9.1.12(2) only Lemma 9.2.7(2): 'a representation ... which satisfies (1), and (2)'. That needs only the K-part. Beyond E137's statement, the lemma really needs E140's fixed-determinant variant with image all of GL_2(F_q). The brief names this variant but never states its conclusions. The fix is still right, and I would apply it. The strong (2) is true. It is what the printed (2) asserts in the case E' = E, which is Calegari's Prop. 3.2. It also makes E140's reason valid. I checked the proposed proof. Take auxiliary places v of E that split completely in E'F^(avoid), hence in E'(zeta_q), since zeta_q lies in F(A[q]) by the Weil pairing. At them, prescribe unramified local extensions whose Frobenii run through every conjugacy class. By (3), a place w of K' above such a v has K'_w = E_v and splits completely in K'F^(avoid). So Frob_w lies in H_0 = Gal(L'/L' cap K'F^(avoid)). In the general form: H = Gal(L'/K') meets every class of G, so H = G by Jordan's lemma. The normal subgroup H_0 then meets every class, so H_0 = G. In the fixed-determinant form: prescribe Frobenii in every GL_2-class contained in SL_2(F_q). H_0 lies in SL_2 and is normal in H. Since q splits completely in K', det(H) = F_q^x, so GL_2 = SL_2 * H and every GL_2-conjugate of H_0 is already an SL_2-conjugate. Hence H_0 meets every SL_2-class, so H_0 = SL_2(F_q) by Jordan's lemma. It follows that H = GL_2(F_q) and L' cap K'F^(avoid) = K'(zeta_q). The right fix has three parts. (a) Restate E137's correction and item 174 as the red team proposes: no L/K; (2) 'K/E is linearly disjoint from E'F^(avoid)/E, and L'/K' is linearly disjoint from K'F^(avoid)/K''; Gal(L'_w/K'_w) in the diagram. (b) In the brief, state the fixed-determinant variant that E140 uses in full: r-bar_q : G_{K'} -> GL_2(F_q) with det r-bar_q = eps-bar^{-1}, image GL_2(F_q), L' cap K'F^(avoid) = K'(zeta_q), and (3)-(5) as before, proved by the auxiliary-place argument above. (c) Do not write into the records that (6) depends on the disjointness. Record instead that the SL_2(F_q) hypothesis of Lemma 7.5.22 follows from full image together with det = eps-bar^{-1}, and that the strong (2) is what E140's reason uses. Classification: this is not a new paper mistake. The paper's mistake is E137, already recorded. This finding is an inconsistency inside the extraction: E137, E140, item 174 and the brief. Medium severity is fair, because item 174 states a false proposition.

Confirmed. I checked Lemma 4.6.24 (published p. 292), its one-line proof 'This follows immediately from an examination of (4.5.12)', and (4.5.12) with its normalisation by p^{-l_w} (p. 277). I also checked the definitions they rely on: omega^kappa, the tensor product over v|p of Sym^{k_v-l_v} omega_{G,v} (x) det^{l_v} omega_{G,v}; the surjection of Corollary 4.3.9 onto the tensor product of the highest-weight lines at all places; and U_{w,2} = U'_w o U''_w. The published text agrees with arXiv v3. At w, the normalised map r_2^* omega -> r_1^* omega is diag(p,1) in bases compatible with the projection to omega_{H,w}. On Sym^{k-l} (x) det^l it acts on e_1^a e_2^{k-l-a} by p^a. It is therefore divisible by p exactly on the kernel at w (a >= 1) and is the identity on the highest-weight line (a = 0). At every v != w the isogeny underlying U'_w and U''_w is an isomorphism of G_v, so the sheaf map there is an isomorphism. The kernel K omega^kappa of the projection at all places contains ker_v (x) (highest-weight line at w) (x) ..., for v != w. On these pieces the sheaf map of U_{w,2} is not divisible by p. The normalised traces cannot supply the missing factor: they are the same traces that make U_{w,2} act on Omega^kappa with nonzero ordinary part. So 'examination of (4.5.12)' proves the per-place claim only when w is the only place above p, which for p split means F = Q, Pilloni's setting. For [F:Q] >= 2 the claim is unproved, and there is no evident reason to expect it. The same computation does prove the product statement. The composite correspondence for prod_{w|p} U_{w,2} has sheaf map (x)_v D_v. Each D_v preserves ker_v and equals p times an integral map on it. So the map is p times an integral map on K omega^kappa, which is the sum of the pieces ker_v (x) (rest), and the traces are integral. Since U^I = prod_{v in I} U_{v,2} prod_{v in I^c} U_{v,1}U_{v,2} (TeX l. 7000) is that product times commuting integral operators, U^I lies in p End. That is exactly the use in Lemma 4.6.25. Nothing else cites Lemma 4.6.24. Item 246 states the per-place form, and no sourceIssue records the problem, so this is a new mistake. The fix is right, with one change of classification. Record it as a gap, but with affects = 'a stated result', not 'nothing'. Lemma 4.6.24 as printed is not established for [F:Q] >= 2, and the correction changes its statement. Say in the reason that nothing downstream changes, because Lemma 4.6.25 needs only prod_{w|p} U_{w,2}, hence U^I, in p End. Restate item 246 accordingly, for both the K omega^kappa complex and its (-D), G_1 variant used in Lemma 4.6.25.

Confirmed. I checked Theorem 8.4.1 and Theorem 8.5.2 with their proofs; the statements are on published pp. 452-453 and 454. The published text matches arXiv v3. Hypotheses (1)-(5) are the similitude, vast and tidy for rho-bar, p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary at v|p, existence of pi with rho-bar_pi ~ rho-bar, and purity at every finite place. (2) and (4) concern only rho-bar, and (3) and (5) are local conditions, place by place. Purity, as defined in §2 following Taylor-Yoshida, is a condition on each local Weil-Deligne representation. So nothing forces rho to be unramified outside a finite set. The paper has no standing convention that would supply it. I searched the TeX for 'unramified outside', 'almost all', 'all but finitely many' and conventions on Galois representations. Where finiteness is needed, the paper states it explicitly: Hypothesis 7.13.1(5) ('There is a finite set R ... if v not in R cup S_p, then rho|G_{F_v} is unramified'), the finite set S in §7.1, and the Patrikis lift in the proof of Lemma 9.2.2 ('unramified at all but finitely many places'). The proof needs the condition twice. It must choose a finite solvable F' so that at every place over a v not dividing p where rho is ramified, rho-bar becomes trivial and q_w = 1 mod p^2. With infinitely many such v, and F' linearly disjoint from F^{ker rho-bar}, Chebotarev makes this impossible in general. The proof then invokes Hypothesis 7.13.1, whose (5) requires the finite set R. Theorem 8.5.2 applies Theorem 8.4.1 to rho|G_{F'} (x) psi^{-1}, so it inherits the gap. Every application in §§9-10 has rho = rho_{A,p}, rho_{B,q}, or a member of a compatible system, all unramified outside a finite set, so no application is affected. Items 118 and 119 copy the printed hypotheses, and no sourceIssue records the problem, so it is new. The fix is right. Record a gap that affects a stated result, repaired by adding 'rho is unramified outside a finite set of places' to both theorems, and add that hypothesis to items 118 and 119.

Confirmed. I checked Theorem 3.10.1 (published p. 236): 'let m be non-Eisenstein', with (1) and (2) stated for H^i(...)_m. Only (3), for i = 0, is stated without localization. I also checked the proof of Proposition 6.6.2 (p. 354): 'Indeed, by Theorem 3.10.1 (2), the cohomology groups on each side can be computed in terms of automorphic representations'. Both passages are the same in arXiv v3. The localization matters. The proof of Theorem 3.10.1 uses it, through Lemma 3.10.7 (H^0(D, omega^kappa)_m = 0), to pass to interior cohomology. The paper says 'This is the only place that we use ... the non-Eisenstein localization', and its introduction warns that the cohomology 'will not generally vanish before localization'. Proposition 6.6.2 is an equality of Euler characteristics, so its proof needs the H^1 comparison. Unlocalized H^1 is not described by Theorem 3.10.1. So Proposition 6.6.2 is unproved as printed, and with it Theorem 6.6.4 (which uses its Euler-characteristic equality) and Theorem 6.6.5 (which uses 6.6.4). Items 287 and 289 notice the dependence in their notes, but no sourceIssue exists, and items 287 and 289-291 state the unlocalized form. So this is new as a record. The later uses are all localized. the proof of Theorem 7.9.4 uses Theorem 6.6.5 localized at m-tilde^{I,alphabeta,Q}; S^{I,alphabeta} in §7.13 is defined as e(U^I)H^0(...)_{m-tilde^{I,alphabeta}}; and the contraction of these ideals to the spherical Hecke algebra away from S is non-Eisenstein because rho-bar is absolutely irreducible. So the main theorems stand. Localizing at m commutes with everything in §6.6, since every map there is equivariant for the prime-to-S spherical Hecke algebra. On the C_p-complexes, read m-localization as the sum of the generalised eigenspaces whose eigensystems reduce to m; the prime-to-p Hecke correspondences preserve the integral models, so these eigenvalues are integral. Localizing also settles the H^1 case of Remark 6.6.3's Katz-Mazur step in the way the authors indicate (item 288). The fix is right, with one addition. Record a gap that affects a stated result (Proposition 6.6.2 and Theorems 6.6.4 and 6.6.5 as stated). Restate items 289-291, and also item 287 (the T/U comparison claim inside the proof, which the finding omits), in the form localized at a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of the spherical Hecke algebra away from S.

Confirmed. I checked Proposition 7.10.1 (published p. 423): 'Let S_infty contains I_1 contains I_2 ... be a decreasing sequence of open ideals of S_infty with cap_N I_N = 0. For each N >= 1 we set S_N = S_infty/I_N', and 'we leave the details of the proof as an exercise'. I also checked §7.11 (pp. 424-425): S_infty = T[[Delta_infty]], a surjection Delta_infty ->> Delta_N is fixed separately for each N with kernel inside (p^N Z_p)^{2q}, and 'We write S_N = T[Delta_N]', followed by 'this data satisfies the assumptions of Proposition 7.10.1'. The published text matches arXiv v3. T is a power series ring over the Iwasawa algebra Lambda_I, so S_N = T[Delta_N] is not Artinian and ker(S_infty -> S_N) is not open. The Taylor-Wiles data Q_N and the surjections are chosen independently for each N, so the kernels are not nested either. The assertion that the data satisfy the hypotheses is therefore false as written. The standard repair works, and I checked it. Put J_N = (m_Lambda^N, x_j^N for the framing variables, (1+y_i)^{p^N} - 1 for a basis delta_i = 1 + y_i of Delta_infty). J_N contains ker(S_infty -> S_N), because that kernel is generated by delta - 1 with delta in ker(Delta_infty -> Delta_N), which lies in (p^N Z_p)^{2q}. J_N is open: it contains a power of pi, and y_i^{p^N} modulo pi. It is decreasing, and cap J_N = 0 because (1+y)^{p^N} - 1 lies in m^{N+1}. Reducing the data modulo J_N keeps modules finite. Freeness is preserved, and so is balancedness: base change does not change dim M/mM and cannot increase dim Tor_1. The lambda-compatibilities pass to the quotients. No sourceIssue records this, and neither item 150 nor item 324 mentions it, so it is new. Item 150 lists R03.5 and P9, while item 324's note says 'R03.5, P8 and P9'. The P8 node 'ultrapatching of perfect complexes' does patch quotients Delta_N with kernel in (p^N Z_p)^{nq} through open J, with two systems identified mod pi. So adding P8 to item 150 is right. The fix is right, with one refinement. Restate item 150 for arbitrary ideals I_N contained in open decreasing J_N with cap J_N = 0, the data being taken modulo J_N, and note in item 324 that I_N = ker(S_infty -> T[Delta_N]) is contained in J_N. On the kind: the sentence claiming the hypotheses hold is a false step, so I would record it as an error that affects the proof. 'Gap' is defensible, since the repair is routine and every conclusion stands.

Checked research/blueprint/queue.json, make_queue.py, lane.py, route 3 and its review. The queue holds two pending design jobs for the same roadmap: DESIGN-BCGP18 (order 3, after []) and DESIGN-AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity (order 142, after []). Both have roadmapIds [AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity], the same four outputs (roadmaps/, packets/, readmes/, suggested/ AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity), and a review job each. BCGP 2025 has the same pair: DESIGN-BCGP25 (order 4, after DESIGN-BCGP18) and DESIGN-AbelianSurfacesModularity (order 143, after []). The cause is as stated. paper_designs names a new-route job DESIGN-<roadmap id>, and main() drops a paper design only when its job id equals a hardcoded job id (d[0]), never when the roadmap id (d[1]) matches. DESIGN_TEMPLATE gives the designer only its BRIEF plus inputs that do not include the paper extractions, and DESIGN-BCGP18 has no promptPreface, so it never sees route 3's brief. That brief says the maintainer attaches it to DESIGN-BCGP18, and the review report says 'DESIGN-BCGP18 should take this file's brief'. lane.claim does not guard against two jobs with the same outputs, so with several lanes the two can run at once, or the later one 'continues' the earlier one's reviewed files under a different brief. BCGP18_BRIEF does contain the quoted sentence inviting a separate higher-Coleman roadmap. It also asks for the Siegel threefold and its compactifications, which route 1's Part II now owns. High severity is right: this changes what gets built. Corrections to the fix: (1) Deduplicating in paper_designs does not remove the twins. make_queue appends to the new queue every old job whose id it no longer produces. The four jobs DESIGN- and REV-DESIGN-AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity, and DESIGN- and REV-DESIGN-AbelianSurfacesModularity, must be set to state 'superseded' in queue.json, and their tracking issues closed. That is a maintainer edit, since workers may not edit the queue. (2) The dedup should key on roadmap id and append to the hardcoded job's brief the paper route's opening plus the pointer to the full brief, as paper_designs already does for proposals. DESIGN-BCGP25 must likewise receive BCGP 2025 route 12's brief. (3) BCGP18_BRIEF should point to route 3 as the binding ownership split. It should drop the higher-Coleman invitation (that theory is route 2's HigherHidaAndColemanTheory) and the Siegel-variety coverage (route 1). (4) If DESIGN-BCGP18 might be claimed before the next regeneration, add the pointer as a promptPreface, which survives regeneration.

I checked every named mistake in the arXiv v3 TeX and the published text. All are present in both versions, and no sourceIssues record has these locators. Theorem 3.5.1(3) (TeX lines 3864-3871, p. 213): on a refinement, pi^*(x_1...x_r) vanishes to order sum a_i >= 2 along the new boundary divisor. For example, in the chart x = a, y = ab one has pi^*(xy) = a^2 b. So only an inclusion holds, and any proper refinement of a smooth fan adds such a ray. Item 43 already states the corrected form and says it 'is recorded as a source issue', but no record exists. Remark 3.9.21 (p. 234): for the paper's J (Section 2.1.1, pairing e1 with e4 and e2 with e3), diag(a,b,c,d) is in GSp_4 exactly when ad = bc. So diag(1,p^-1,p^-1,p^-1) and diag(1,1,1,p^-1) are not in GSp_4(F_w), although their product is. Remark 7.5.23 against Section 7.5.20 (pp. 398-401): |Sp_4(F_3)| = 51840 = 2^7*3^4*5, so the subgroups of order 128 are the Sylow 2-subgroups and form one class. I also computed directly that Q_8 wr Z/2 in Sp_4(F_3) is enormous. (E1) holds because its order is prime to 3. (E2) holds because the commutant of V is 1-dimensional. (E3) holds: ad^0 has 4 simple types, and the submodule generated by the fixed vectors of the 48 elements with four distinct eigenvalues is all of ad^0. So the list is right and the remark's last sentence is false. Section 6.5.1 (p. 339): deg M is defined with truncated v(x_i mod p), and delta_H is put in det omega_G' (x) det omega_G^-1. Pull-back along G -> G' gives a section of det omega_G (x) det omega_G'^-1: for mu_p in mu_{p^inf} it is multiplication by p, with valuation 1 = deg mu_p, and the printed direction would give p^-1, which is not integral. Items 144 and 264 copy the inverted bundle and silently correct the degree.
